mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% in three-month window
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand for goods and services, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases financing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 4.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a statistical artifact or data inconsistency rather than genuine labor market strength, which historically has coincided with market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases over two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals weakening residential construction activity, which negatively impacts homebuilding and related sectors, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.
